question: What does Parpola 2019 mean by sign no. 41, and does it source the H-2148 local 110 branch?
result: Parpola 2019's sign-list convention is sourced to Parpola 1994, pp. 70-78, Fig. 5.1. In the downloaded Parpola 1994 PDF, sign no. 41 is visible on printed p. 70 / PDF page 88 and includes the kneeling/person-with-raised-object variant matching Parpola 2019's prose. This resolves the article-convention gate but does not accept local 110 as Parpola sign no. 41.
observations: Parpola 2019 says the paper quotes sign numbers from Parpola 1994, pp. 70-78, Fig. 5.1.
Parpola 2019 describes the H-940/H-2147/H-2148 reverse-side sign no. 41 as a kneeling man holding a pot.
Parpola 1994 Fig. 5.1 sign no. 41 has variants a-f, including a solid kneeling/person-with-raised-object variant.
Mayig V041 maps to P301, a small hatched box, and is not visually the Parpola 1994 sign no. 41 family.
Mayig P041 maps to V141/W112/M034 and remains rejected as a numeric shortcut.
The H-2148 one-sign panel is visually compatible with the Parpola sign no. 41 family, but current public crop quality is not enough for closed identification.
next_gate: Acquire or inspect independent H-2148/H2001-5142 same-side evidence tying the one-sign panel to the reverse side and to Parpola 1994 sign no. 41, while preserving local row 481.2 +110+ as an unaccepted crosswalk candidate.
